start.title: Borrowed Gloves
start.text: A stable girl catches you near the trough and asks, with practiced casualness, whether you have an old pair of gloves you no longer need. Her own are patched through at two fingertips.

choices.text: Notice what she is not saying

buckets.flavourText: The exposed fingertips are pale and waxy rather than merely red. She has been working with early frostbite.
The request sounds simple enough: gloves wear out quickly around reins, buckles, and frozen water.

choices.text: Offer your spare gloves if you have them

frostbite.title: More Than Worn Cloth
frostbite.text: When you ask to see her hand, she tries to laugh it off. Feeling has only partly returned to two fingers since morning.

choices.text: Wrap her hands with your clean bandage
Show her how to warm them safely

buckets.flavourText: You stop her from rubbing the skin and get the hand wrapped in dry wool instead.
Your advice is more confident than precise. The cook overhears and sends her to the herb-wife.

choices.text: Send her straight to the herb-wife

choice.title: A Small Request
choice.text: She waits, clearly prepared for either answer.

give.title: Hands Inside Wool
give.text: The gloves are too large, which seems to delight her. She curls both hands into fists and says she will return them when the thaw comes, as if that were a reasonable date.

patch.title: Needle Work
patch.text: You take the gloves and spend part of the evening reinforcing the fingers with scraps of leather. The result is ugly and warmer than before.

helped.title: Warmth, Slowly
helped.text: Colour begins returning to her fingers. She promises, reluctantly, to finish the shift indoors.

herbwife.title: Someone Who Knows Better
herbwife.text: The herb-wife takes one look and starts issuing orders. The stable girl shoots you an accusing glance, but she keeps the hand in the warm wrap.

refuse.title: No Spare Pair
refuse.text: You tell her you cannot help. She nods as if she expected that and returns to breaking ice from the trough.
